\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{إلغاء} (ilghāʾ)}{إلغاء (ilghāʾ)}]{\ar{إلغاء} (ilghāʾ) — a cancellation}

\label{lesson:AR-C461-ilgha}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to go bad, then the Arabic for to suffer damage.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{إلغاء}}
\textbf{\ar{إلغاء}} — \emph{ilghāʾ} — \textquotedblleft{}a cancellation\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{سمعنا} \ar{عن} \ar{إلغاء} \ar{الرحلة} \ar{في} \ar{المطار}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{samiʿnā ʿan ilghāʾ ar-riḥla fī al-maṭār.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We heard about the cancellation of the flight at the airport.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{إلغاء}} (\emph{ilghāʾ}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{l-gh-w}, \textquotedblleft{}to be of no account\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is the verbal noun of Form IV, \textquotedblleft{}to make null\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ilghāʾ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ilghāʾ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{samiʿnā ʿan ilghāʾ ar-riḥla fī al-maṭār.} — We heard about the cancellation of the flight at the airport.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to go bad, then the Arabic for to suffer damage, then say \emph{ilghāʾ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{إلغاء} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A cancellation\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تأجيل} (taʾjīl)}{تأجيل (taʾjīl)}]{\ar{تأجيل} (taʾjīl) — a postponement}

\label{lesson:AR-C461-tajil}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to suffer damage, then the Arabic for a cancellation.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تأجيل}}
\textbf{\ar{تأجيل}} — \emph{taʾjīl} — \textquotedblleft{}a postponement\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{أخبرنا} \ar{المدير} \ar{بتأجيل} \ar{الاجتماع}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{akhbaranā al-mudīr bi-taʾjīl al-ijtimāʿ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The manager told us the meeting was postponed.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تأجيل}} (\emph{taʾjīl}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʾ-j-l}, \textquotedblleft{}an appointed term\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is the verbal noun of Form II, \textquotedblleft{}to set a later term\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taʾjīl}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to suffer damage, then the Arabic for a cancellation, then say \emph{taʾjīl} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{فوت} (fawwata)}{فوت (fawwata)}]{\ar{فوت} (fawwata) — to miss (a chance); to let slip}

\label{lesson:AR-C461-fawwata}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a postponement, then the Arabic for to cancel.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{فوت}}
\textbf{\ar{فوت}} — \emph{fawwata} — \textquotedblleft{}to miss (a chance); to let slip\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{فوت} \ar{أخي} \ar{الحفلة} \ar{بسبب} \ar{العمل}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{fawwata akhī al-ḥafla bi-sabab al-ʿamal.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My brother missed the party because of work.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يفوت}, \emph{yufawwit}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{فوت}} (\emph{fawwata}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{f-w-t}, \textquotedblleft{}to pass by, to escape\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form II, \textquotedblleft{}to let pass\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{ضيع} (ḍayyaʿa)}{ضيع (ḍayyaʿa)}]{\ar{ضيع} (ḍayyaʿa) — to waste time; to lose}

\label{lesson:AR-C461-dayyaa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to cancel, then the Arabic for to miss.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{ضيع}}
\textbf{\ar{ضيع}} — \emph{ḍayyaʿa} — \textquotedblleft{}to waste time; to lose\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{ضيعنا} \ar{ساعة} \ar{في} \ar{الازدحام}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ḍayyaʿnā sāʿa fī al-izdiḥām.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We wasted an hour in the traffic jam.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يضيع}, \emph{yuḍayyiʿ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{ضيع}} (\emph{ḍayyaʿa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ḍ-y-ʿ}, \textquotedblleft{}to be lost, to perish\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form II, \textquotedblleft{}to let be lost\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}
